title: the in-place Reed-Solomon decode writes its parity bytes at a fixed offset past the output buffer
live_proof: absent at the pin: v4.6.8 carries the fix's renamed constant PFT_RS_K_MAX and the widened allocation 'wmem_alloc(pinfo->pool, decoded_size + PFT_RS_N - rsk)' at :407, and the vulnerable 'memcpy(output+index_out+PFT_RS_N_MAX, ...)' has zero occurrences there. The triage script found 6 of 6 of the fix's distinctive added lines already in v4.6.8. A fix-reversal. The pre-fix shape is quoted from e8ef9df09d^:epan/dissectors/packet-dcp-etsi.c:235-237 (the swapped constants), :264 (the parity copy), :270 (index_out += rsk) and :376 (the allocation).
object: the RS output buffer, fcount*plen bytes in the packet scope
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. Spatial row.
shape: fixed-offset parity write lands past the buffer, inside the same block
allocator_layer: block_fast -- the packet scope (pinfo->pool); the firing bound is wm_narrow()'s.
fidelity: model-consumer, real allocator. The RS decode is reduced to the FIRST byte its parity copy writes past the buffer (index_out = 0, offset PFT_RS_N_MAX); eras_dec_rs and the deinterleave are dropped because they do not touch the bound.
distinguishing: the first row in this corpus whose stale access is a WRITE rather than a read, so it is the one that exercises the write probe and oracle_site's site-1 path.

spatial.oracle: fault at the labelled write probe
spatial.note: Every arm of this harness narrows a wmem allocation to its request -- ports/wireshark/wmem/src/shared/wmem-port-hooks.h:11-15, wm_narrow(), unconditional under WM_DOMAIN -- so a spatial crossing faults on all of them and this case does NOT discriminate the chunk port. Established by case 13, whose completion predictions the run refuted; these four are pre-registered with that correction already applied. PREDICTION REFUTED BY THE RUN, 2026-10-05: this arm was pre-registered with cause 5, the LOAD access fault. A bounds violation on a STORE raises cause 7, and the run read 7 at exactly the predicted write-probe pc. Corrected to 7. The two read rows (13, 14, 15) do read 5, so the pre-registration was right about the probe and wrong about load-vs-store.

poisoncap-spatial.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured: faults if mode 0 bounds each wmem chunk, completes if it bounds only the g_malloc'd block. Neither platform is on this host; the reading settles it.

poisoncap-protected.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured: mode 1 adds temporal protection and no lifetime ends here, so the spatial behaviour of mode 0 decides it.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: PREDICTED, not measured: completes. CHERI bounds the g_malloc'd block and the crossing stays inside it; the revoker has nothing to sweep because nothing is freed.
cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with the guest's own libc revocation on

native-detect.oracle: NO ASan report: the crossing stays inside the one g_malloc'd block, so there is no redzone between the chunks to poison. A silent arm needs its own positive control -- a crossing past the END of the block, which ASan must report -- before it means anything.

status: PRE-REGISTERED 2026-10-05 with cause 5 and CORRECTED to cause 7 by the run: a bounds violation on a STORE is cause 7, not the load fault's 5. Measured at the predicted write-probe pc on both builds. Re-run after the correction is the recorded reading; see the result bundle.
